title: Coronation Street Fans Say the 1 Death the Show Got Wrong
metaDescription: Coronation Street fans still argue the soap got one major death wrong, and the cast member behind it agrees the exit felt rushed.
author: EpisodeLens Staff
altText: Coronation Street fans discuss the Kylie Platt death scene outside the Rovers Return
html:
Coronation Street fans have long memories, and few things unite them faster than an argument about a death that never should have happened. The cobbles have buried dozens of characters over six decades, but one exit still gets brought up in fan forums and Facebook groups more than almost any other.

That exit belongs to Kylie Platt, played by Paula Lane. When Kylie was stabbed to death in 2016 by Clayton Hibbs, Coronation Street fans were left stunned. It wasn't just the shock of losing a long-running character. It was the timing. Kylie had finally turned her life around, settled into married life with David, and seemed ready for a quieter chapter.

Why Coronation Street Fans Still Debate Kylie Platt's Exit

Paula Lane had already told producers she planned to leave the show after six years. That part was never a secret. What bothered viewers was how quickly the writing moved once the decision was made. Kylie's redemption arc, built patiently over years, ended in a single violent night outside the Rovers.

Lane herself has spoken about it since. In later interviews she said she was happy with how Kylie went out, calling it a strong exit for a character she loved playing. Not every cast member gets that kind of send-off, and she knew it.

Still, the debate hasn't faded. Coronation Street fans point out that David Platt's grief storyline ran for years afterward, shaping everything from his marriage to his feud with Clayton. In hindsight, that long shadow is exactly why some viewers wish Kylie had been given a slower, less brutal ending.

What Paula Lane Did After Weatherfield

Lane didn't disappear after leaving the ITV soap. She moved straight into theatre work, then joined Emmerdale as Ella Forster in 2024. That switch made her one of a small group of actors to appear in both of Britain's biggest soaps.

For Coronation Street fans, seeing her pop up in another village was strange at first. But it also proved the point she made after Kylie's death: the exit wasn't a career ending, just a chapter closing.

She has also been open about how physically demanding the stabbing scenes were. Filming Kylie's final moments took hours, and the emotional weight stayed with her for a while afterward.

The Real Reason the Death Still Stings

It comes down to wasted potential. Kylie had just started working at the salon, repairing her relationship with David, and building something stable for her kids. Killing her at that exact moment felt less like a tragedy and more like a shortcut.

Compare that with other major Weatherfield deaths. Hayley Cropper's exit was planned for months, with a full storyline about her illness and a quiet, devastating goodbye. Kylie got a knife and a pavement.

That contrast is what Coronation Street fans keep coming back to. They aren't angry that she died. They're angry that she died before the show let her breathe.

Would the Show Do It Differently Now?

Modern soaps have shifted. Long-running characters now tend to get extended farewell arcs, complete with callbacks and proper goodbyes. If Kylie's exit were written today, it would likely stretch across several weeks instead of one brutal episode.

Lane has never said she regrets leaving. She has said she'd return if the story made sense, though David has since remarried and moved on. That door stays slightly open, which is more than most dead soap characters get.

For now, the argument lives on in comment sections. Every time a Weatherfield death airs, someone brings up Kylie. That's the strange legacy of a character killed off eight years ago and still argued about like it happened last week.

What do you think? Did Coronation Street get Kylie's exit right, or was it too soon?
